claims.claim: In the committed backtest report reports/verify-2026-06-25.json, 13 of the 20 recommended repositories had gained at least 10% more stars since the day they were recommended. The report used a 7-day report filter, but every entry was observed one day after discovery (days_since_discovery: 1), so the measured growth horizon is roughly one day.
claims.metric: share of recommended repositories whose star count grew by at least 10% within the backtest window, at a score threshold of 90
claims.method: scripts/verify_scoring.py reads the committed daily reports in data/discovery-*.json, takes stars_at_discovery from them, compares against the repository's current star count, and counts a repository as taking off at growth_rate >= 0.1. The '7-day' label describes the report filter: --days 7 selected which daily reports to read, and all 20 sampled entries came from the 2026-06-24/25 reports with days_since_discovery: 1, so growth was observed over roughly one day, not seven.
claims.repro_caveat: re-runs the methodology over the 7-day window relative to today and recomputes growth against today's star counts; it does not reproduce the 2026-06-25 figures, because that snapshot's input reports are no longer committed under data/.

claims.claim: Recommended repositories in that same backtest sample grew 18.71% on average, or 309 stars per day.
claims.metric: mean star growth rate and mean absolute daily star growth across the 20 repositories in the backtest sample (roughly one day of observed growth)
claims.method: same run as backtest-precision-7d; reported as avg_growth_rate_all and avg_daily_growth in the metrics block of the report
claims.repro_caveat: re-runs the methodology over the 7-day window relative to today and recomputes growth against today's star counts; it does not reproduce the 2026-06-25 figures, because that snapshot's input reports are no longer committed under data/.

claims.claim: The recall and lift figures in that backtest report are not usable as evidence, because every repository in the sample scored at or above the threshold.
claims.metric: size of the below-threshold comparison group in the backtest sample
claims.method: the report's own metrics block records high_score_count 20 and low_score_count 0, so recall 1.0 and lift "inf" are arithmetic artifacts of an empty comparison group rather than measurements of discrimination
